n: The Lord addresses the priests directly with a warning.
If they won’t listen and honor God’s name from the heart, He will turn their blessings — perhaps the priestly blessings they pronounce — into curses. It has already begun.

A shocking image: God will rebuke their descendants and smear their faces with the refuse from their own festival sacrifices, and they will be carried out with it. Their unworthy worship will disgrace them.

f.g: The offal from sacrificed animals, normally burned outside the camp (Exodus 29:14).

n: Then they’ll know God sent this warning to keep His covenant with Levi, the priestly tribe.

f.w: my covenant might be with Levi

n: God’s covenant with Levi brought life and peace, given because Levi reverenced God.
A portrait of a true priest: he taught truth, spoke no lies, walked with God in peace and uprightness, and turned many from sin. A model for every teacher of God’s word.

f.w: did turn many away from iniquity

n: A priest’s lips should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from him, for he is the Lord’s messenger.

f.w: the priest's lips should keep knowledge
the messenger of the LORD of hosts
f.g: Hebrew mal’ak — the same word as in Malachi’s name.

n: But these priests have left the path, caused many to stumble by their teaching, and corrupted Levi’s covenant.

f.w: ye have caused many to stumble

n: So God has made them despised before the people, because they showed favoritism in applying the law.

f.g: Showing favoritism; bending rules for some.

n: Don’t we all have one Father? Didn’t one God create us? Why then betray one another and break our ancestors’ covenant? A foundation for treating everyone as family.

f.w: Have we not all one father?

f.g: Act faithlessly; break faith. The word appears five times in verses 10–16.

n: Judah has been unfaithful — profaning God’s holy place and marrying women who worship foreign gods. This drew people away from the covenant.

f.w: married the daughter of a strange god

n: God will cut off anyone who does this from Israel’s community, no matter who they are, even if they bring offerings.

f.g: Literally “he who wakes and he who answers” — meaning everyone, without exception.

n: They flood the altar with tears and wailing because God no longer accepts their offerings — but they don’t see why.

f.w: covering the altar of the LORD with tears
f.g: Perhaps also the tears of wives they had abandoned.

n: Here’s why: God witnessed the marriage covenant they made with the wife of their youth, and they betrayed her. She is your partner and your covenant wife. God takes marriage covenants seriously.

f.g: Marriage is a covenant made before God.

n: Didn’t God make husband and wife one, with a portion of His Spirit? Why one? Because He seeks godly children. So guard your spirit and stay faithful to your wife. A difficult Hebrew verse, but its message is clear.
The Lord says He hates divorce, and the one who abandons his wife covers himself with violence like a garment. Guard your heart and don’t break faith.

f.g: “Putting away” means divorcing — here abandoning a faithful spouse.

n: You’ve wearied the Lord with your words. How? By claiming evildoers are good in God’s eyes, or asking, “Where is the God of justice?” This cynical question sets up God’s answer in chapter 3.

f.w: Ye have wearied the LORD with your words
Where is the God of judgment?
